newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada T-bills open firmer amid gains in currency.
newsitem.headline: Canada T-bills open firmer amid gains in currency.

text.p: Canadian T-bills opened mostly firmer in quiet trade on Thursday, helped by strength in the Canadian dollar and the recent sharp gains in U.S. fixed-income markets, analysts said.

"We have renewed interest in this market on a number of issues. One is the seemingly building bullish sentiment in the U.S. That's giving us a lot of direction here. And we've got the currency strength," said Walter Posiewko, a money market trader with Royal Bank Investment Management Inc.
Canada's three-month when-issued T-bill firmed to yield 3.16 percent from 3.18 percent at Wednesday's close.
